summary: Angola’s restoration pledges centre on forest recovery, with separate reforestation figures ranging from 227,000 to 1,246,700 hectares and assisted forest regeneration reported at 1,068,497 and 1,246,700 hectares. The 1,246,700-hectare figure equals about 1.6% of the country’s current 759,359 km² forest area. A separate 10-year programme targets 2% of national territory, estimated at 2,493,400 hectares, and a mixed restoration–agriculture commitment applies reforestation with agroforestry to 500 hectares, about 0.008% of current agricultural land. Conservation pledges include avoiding deforestation across 555,000 hectares, about 0.7% of current forest, and potentially avoiding 387,000 tCO2e annually through improved fire management in Cuando Cubango peatland zones.
